answer:
ANSWER: **Final vs Baseline Blood** shows negligible effects.

IMPORTANT CORRECTION to the plan (the mapping is resolved, not hand-waved):
The 9 pre-computed DESeq comparisons in the file are NOT the 3 tissue comparisons. I mapped them explicitly (log2FC correlation, verified by U/D direction). They are **response-group comparisons WITHIN each tissue** (3 tissues × {good-vs-Control, bad-vs-Control, good-vs-bad}):

  Comp  A (resp/tissue)      B (resp/tissue)      corr   verify U^/Dv
  1     good/baseline        Control/baseline     0.544  0.86/0.88
  2     bad/baseline         Control/baseline     0.675  0.92/1.00
  3     good/baseline        bad/baseline         0.668  0.97/0.99
  4     good/dentate         Control/dentate      0.604  0.91/1.00
  5     bad/dentate          Control/dentate      0.597  0.99/0.88
  6     good/dentate         bad/dentate          0.687  0.93/1.00
  7     good/final           Control/final        0.721  1.00/1.00
  8     bad/final            Control/final        0.717  1.00/1.00
  9     good/final           bad/final            0.713  1.00/1.00

The mapping is unambiguous (perfectly regular; U-genes higher in A and D-genes lower in A in 86–100% of cases). CONSEQUENCE: none of the 9 is a tissue-vs-tissue comparison, so the 3 target tissue comparisons are NOT in the file and MUST be computed from the CPM counts. Therefore the "authors' U/D as primary" cannot be applied to the tissue comparisons (their U/D columns belong to the response comparisons); instead I applied the authors' reverse-engineered DEG rule (padj<0.05 & |log2FC|>0.5) plus sensitivity thresholds, to my computed tissue comparisons. This is why the "from-scratch recompute" is the primary analysis here, not a cross-check.

DE METHOD: R/DESeq2 unavailable in the runner → Welch (independent) and within-subject paired t-tests on log2(CPM+1) per gene, BH-FDR. 30 vs 30 samples per comparison (10 per response, pooled); fully paired design (30/30 subjects in all 3 tissues). Independent and paired give identical conclusions.

FULL UP/DOWN + BINOMIAL (two-sided exact, p0=0.5, α=0.05), independent model:
  Comparison            rule               n_up  n_dn    n     binom_p   up%
  Final vs Baseline     padj<0.05           4405  5597 10002   9.0e-33   44.0
  Final vs Baseline     padj<.05&|fc|>=.5   2159  1748  3907   5.2e-11   55.3
  Final vs Baseline     padj<.05&|fc|>=1     615   244   859   1.1e-37   71.6
  Final vs Baseline     padj<.05&|fc|>=2      16    24    40   0.268     40.0  <-- balanced/NS
  Dentate vs Baseline   padj<0.05          10862  8551 19413   7.1e-62   55.9
  Dentate vs Baseline   padj<.05&|fc|>=.5   9086  7236 16322   1.4e-47   55.7
  Dentate vs Baseline   padj<.05&|fc|>=1    7134  5481 12615   4.2e-49   56.5
  Dentate vs Baseline   padj<.05&|fc|>=2    4759  3170  7929   1.3e-71   60.0
  Dentate vs Final      padj<0.05          11088  8080 19168   5.1e-105  57.8
  Dentate vs Final      padj<.05&|fc|>=.5   9298  6939 16237   1.0e-76   57.3
  Dentate vs Final      padj<.05&|fc|>=1    7344  5332 12676   1.2e-71   57.9
  Dentate vs Final      padj<.05&|fc|>=2    4886  3254  8140   1.6e-73   60.0
(Paired model: same calls; e.g. Final vs Baseline |fc|>=2 still 16/24, p=0.268.)

OPERATIONAL DEFINITION OF "NEGLIGIBLE": the comparison whose up/down DEG balance does NOT reject H0(p_up=0.5) in the two-sided exact binomial test at α=0.05 (i.e., no significant directional bias). Total-DEG counts are reported above so the call is not just "fewest genes."

WHY Final vs Baseline Blood:
- It has the FEWEST DEGs at every threshold (10002/3907/859/40 vs ~19000/16000/12500/8000 for both dentate comparisons).
- It is the MOST balanced up/down (44–55% up, closest to 50%); the dentate comparisons are consistently the MOST skewed (56–60% up) AND the most numerous.
- It is the ONLY comparison that reaches a non-significant (balanced) binomial test: at |log2FC|>=2, 16 up vs 24 down, p=0.268 (NS). Both dentate-gyrus-vs-blood comparisons stay extremely significant (p<=1.6e-71) — they are dominated by tissue-identity differences (brain region vs blood), not by a small treatment effect.
So the "negligible" call is supported by BOTH fewest-DEGs and most-balanced-up/down (independent signals), not by accident.

FINAL: Final vs Baseline Blood — binomial p=0.268 (balanced, non-significant) at the 4-fold DEG threshold; it is the least-affected comparison (fewest DEGs, highest binomial p) at all thresholds.
